status: Retained stencil point/radius repair: DRC/consumer validation and capability/full-fixture cost gates pass. The observed full-fixture layer-order/marker variation is reproduced and documented. The complete properties.md goal remains active.
scope: Native stencil pad-pair candidates, checked point-radius decisions, drill matching, and finite via report anchors.

baseline.result: Two ordinary-input projection panics, an unresolved pad-pair radius treated as a definite finding, an unresolved matching radius arm, and two unresolved drill-match fallbacks. Five existing controls pass; they are not counted as repaired failures.

contract: points_within_radius checks native squared distance against squared radius under STRICT, with a separate negative-radius decision. Required orders and known exhausted scopes return typed failure; no optional square-root result can silently remove a pair.

Native stencil centers and radius use certified outward enclosures in the same EnvelopeSpatialIndex as native layer polygons. Missing or nonrepresentable projections retain candidates. Each enclosure covers every cell between endpoint keys; oversized storage/query boxes use the existing 256-cell fallback. No report coordinate or one-ULP heuristic excludes stencil points.

The shared grid is factored into checks/spatial/envelope.rs; polygon semantics and deterministic candidate sorting/deduplication are retained. If no envelope has positive span, cell size uses the nominal radius and grid floor rather than a default span of one.

Drill matching skips irrelevant unplated/net-mismatched drills before requesting numeric certificates. Required matching-radius and point-distance orders are checked. An unknown earlier match cannot be skipped to select a later drill or copper fallback; a known first match does not inspect later drills.

Via report anchors use checked finite projection. An unrepresentable anchor emits geometry uncertainty instead of panicking. The public BoardModel permits anchors independent of geometry; the regression exercises that boundary explicitly.
Unresolved stencil geometry produces a blocking Uncertain readiness receipt. Implementation version advances from 7 to 8; schema remains 1.

consumer_validation.scope: Six Easyduino snapshots, one impedance unit and two smoke tests selected by hyperdrc, plus five curved-outline tests. This is not the complete HyperCircuit suite.

cost.limitations: Five sequential fresh processes pinned to CPU 0 after all builds/tests exit. The first 32 witnesses and iteration counts repeat the prior bounds/area/operation probe unchanged. Eight new rows time complete stencil checks, including native enclosure grid construction, candidate predicates, coverage geometry and report allocation. Inputs are fixed; first/last native area/report witnesses and full serialized-finding fingerprints are outside timers, as is fixture construction. Internal geometry evidence may be warm. The sparse tombstone case retains all 1,002 pads and its single qualifying imbalance. Report rows include a valid matching drill, an unresolved drill match and a nonrepresentable marker. All 40 witness rows must match across five trials; this is capability cost, not a matched speedup or allocation/library-size comparison. The million-sample report fixture is included in whole-process RSS. The full two-board/Gerber fixture workload and 120-second gate are unchanged.

Shared guards reject known exhausted scopes; they do not establish total runtime, memory or precision bounds.

fixture_finding_audit.status: passed with documented existing layer-order/marker variation
fixture_finding_audit.scope: All nine logged check counts are unchanged. Every rendered finding other than the duplicate-layer row matches after path/ID and row-order normalization. The duplicate compares the same In1.Cu/B.Cu sets and emits the same polygon/message, but its layer order and eight optional markers change. An isolated full-board replay of both input orders reproduces both variants. BoardModel::copper_layers and layer-check source files are byte-identical to the pre-stencil commit. The former iterates a HashMap; the duplicate check takes markers from the left source. Both parsed native layers have area 10000 and empty symmetric difference. No deterministic whole-report, original ID or optional-marker identity claim is made.
